focus.jtag: Reports of fresh U.S./Israeli strikes on Iran spiked oil (Brent ~$111–113, WTI ~$99) and knocked tech futures; the AI trade re-cracked after Tesla/Meta. The scanner boarded three Type A post-earnings gaps — GGG, IBM, MEDP — all bearish, all on near-zero relative volume
focus.jnote: The environment turned defensive overnight. Futures came under pressure as escalating concern about Mideast conflict pushed oil higher and spurred inflation fears with the midterms under two weeks away; Nasdaq-100 futures slid about 1.9% and S&P 500 futures dropped around 1% early in New York. Oil climbed on worries over escalation as the U.S. reportedly plans to resume strikes against Iran — Brent rose ~2.7% to ~$111.74 and WTI gained ~2.2% to ~$99.30. By 8 a.m. ET Brent had reached ~$113.21 per barrel. On top of the oil shock, futures fell led by tech as investors digested Tesla and Meta earnings and oil surged to a five-month high. Volatility expanded: VIX was ~18.17, up ~9%, the 10-year near 5.15%, and gold fell ~1.8% to ~$4,076. This is a live, open-ended geopolitical/oil tail stacked on an AI-earnings wobble — not a premium-selling tape.
focus.notdown: None of the three boarded names is a clean bull-put — all three are bearish Type A gaps, and the tape is risk-off. The only groups catching a bid are energy (on the oil spike) and defensives like staples/pharma — but those are two-sided war/oil trades, not clean Snipers: one de-escalation headline gaps crude back down fast. On a HOT, oil-shock morning the disciplined answer is watch-only, sell nothing new.
focus.notup: The bearish side is where the three boarded gaps sit — GGG, IBM and MEDP — but every one printed on near-zero relative volume, and one (IBM) outright conflicts with the tape. GGG fell ~9.2% after hours on a genuine Q3 miss (adjusted EPS $0.81 vs $0.84, revenue $586.4M vs ~$591M). But IBM BEAT (adjusted EPS $2.95 vs $2.86) and its shares closed up ~4% at ~$251.49 — the scanner's bearish IBM row disagrees with reality, so treat it as flagged, not a trade. Selling bear calls into a VIX-rising, oil-shock tape invites a violent squeeze on any peace headline — stand aside.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite ~71 is into HOT and P(≥1% gap) at ~48% is well above the 35% trigger — either alone locks out GREEN. More important than the numbers: an oil supply shock on live Iran-strike reports is an unscheduled, open-ended tail, and the three boarded names are all bearish gaps on near-zero relative volume — none clears the 1.3× confirmation bar, and the IBM row contradicts the actual print (a beat that traded up). Stand down on new credit spreads, or if you must be positioned, push DTE past the conflict window and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

setups.read: The scanner's top-graded name — a Type A gap DOWN that the tape actually backs. Graco reported adjusted EPS of $0.81, missing the $0.84 consensus by three cents, and revenue of $586.4M that fell short of the ~$591M consensus. Shares fell ~9.2% after hours on the miss (the stock fell ~8.4% after the release), with the scanner's indication near ~$75.69 vs the ~$81.81 prior close and four S/R layers within 7%. But the catch the scanner flagged: the reaction printed on near-zero relative volume (0.00×, far below the 1.3× bar), the options-implied move was 5.7% vs a ~7.5% realized gap, and no open-interest data returned — verify the chain manually. setups.read: Flagged — this bearish row conflicts with the actual print; do NOT trade it as written. The scanner boarded IBM bearish (gap down, prior close 251.46, guidance-cut note), but the tape says the opposite: IBM’s adjusted EPS of $2.95 BEAT the $2.86 consensus by 3.15%, with revenue of $17.1B beating by ~1.66%. IBM shares closed the regular session at $251.49, up ~3.96%. Full-year revenue guidance was maintained while free-cash-flow guidance was raised, and the stock traded up ~7.4% to ~$269.50 immediately after reporting. A beat-and-up print is not a valid bear-call setup; the scanner’s “guidance cut” note is unsupported. Treat as INVALID — the direction is wrong and relative volume was near zero (0.05×).
setups.check_note: Stand aside — the bias conflicts with the tape. IBM beat and traded UP, so a bear call fails 4-VAL’s premise. Do not enter. If anything, the real post-earnings reaction is bullish; wait for a fresh, correctly-biased scan. No earnings inside DTE (next ~Jan 2027) if ever reconsidered.

setups.read: A tricky Type A — graded B, and a “guide-light” fade on an earnings beat. Medpace shares slipped ~1.9% after hours as its full-year revenue guidance disappointed, even though results beat. GAAP net income was $137.5M, or $4.84 per diluted share, surpassing the $4.44 estimate, while FY26 revenue guidance of $2.835–$2.855B had a midpoint below the ~$2.852B consensus. The bearish lean rests on the soft revenue guide, not a clean miss — fragile, especially since the options-implied move was 12.1% vs only a ~3.1% realized gap. The scanner also flagged it printed on near-zero relative volume (0.01×) and liquidity was NOT verified — ATM spread and OI must be confirmed before any entry. On a RED day, watch-only.

risks: Fresh U.S./Israeli strikes on Iran — oil climbed as the U.S. reportedly plans to resume strikes against Iran. Any actual strike or Gulf retaliation gaps the whole tape instantly — the number-one thing to watch.

Oil & Strait of Hormuz — Brent rose ~2.7% to ~$111.74 and WTI ~2.2% to ~$99.30, and Brent reached ~$113.21 by 8 a.m. ET. Any shipping incident sends crude (and jet fuel) vertical — the week’s biggest tail.

AI trade re-cracks — futures fell led by tech as investors digested Tesla and Meta earnings and oil surged to a five-month high; Nasdaq-100 futures declined ~1.7% as semiconductor stocks fell. A continued chip rollover drags the whole index.

10Y near 5.15% on the oil shock — the 10-year sat near 5.15% (up ~3 bps) with the VIX ~18.17 and gold off ~1.8%. A rate pop stacked on the oil move compounds pressure on stocks; the Fed is in blackout before the Oct 27–28 FOMC.

Thin volume & a bad bias on the boarded names — GGG (0.00×), IBM (0.05×) and MEDP (0.01×) all printed well below the 1.3× bar, and the IBM row is bearish while IBM actually beat and traded UP. Treat all three as half-size, confirm-at-9:35 watch-items at best; stand aside on IBM entirely.
